summary: This section explains what the Central Government can do after reading an inspector's report. It allows the government to prosecute guilty persons, start winding up proceedings for companies, or file applications for recovering lost property and taking back undue benefits gained through fraud. All company officers and employees must help the government with these prosecutions.
points: The Central Government may prosecute any person found criminally liable based on the report.
Company officers and employees must give necessary assistance for the prosecution.
The government may petition the Tribunal to wind up a company or apply under section 241.
The government may bring proceedings in the name of the company to recover damages or misapplied property in the public interest.
The company must pay back or indemnify the government for any costs spent on those proceedings.
The government may apply to the Tribunal for disgorgement of undue benefits taken due to fraud and hold persons personally liable without limit.
example: A special report on Alpha Traders Private Limited showed that a director had misused company funds for personal gain and committed fraud. Based on this report, the Central Government decided to take action. First, the government filed an application before the Tribunal asking for the disgorgement of the cash and property taken by the director, seeking to hold him personally liable without any limit. Second, because the company was in a poor state due to these issues, the government authorized a person to present a petition to the Tribunal for the winding up of Alpha Traders Private Limited. Throughout this process, all employees and officers of the company had a legal duty to give the Central Government all necessary assistance.

terms.meaning: To start a legal case in court against someone accused of a crime.
The legal process of closing down a company and settling its affairs.
Wrongdoing or improper conduct while performing official duties.
Giving up illegally obtained profits or assets by court order.

watch: Note that the Central Government can either prosecute individuals for crimes or start civil proceedings to recover company property, depending on what the inspector's report reveals.
